PASS for the continuation99 PARTIAL join: sections 1–4 establish first membership, the pullback identification, normalized compactness, and precisely the countable antecedent E of actual86. This certifies no original P16.1 closure. The accepted mathematical bodies are used within their specified bindings; their historical verdicts, hashes, and diagnostics supply no additional inference.

Resolution and descent. The hypotheses of [Temkin 1.2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0904.1592v2#page=3) hold: X is Noetherian, excellent, integral, generically reduced, and over Q. Its blowups are projective. Their Rees algebras remain integral, and they preserve the dense regular locus, so the resulting morphism is birational with integral projective source. Regularity implies smoothness over the perfect field k. Pullback of a globally generated tensor power of L proves that M=pi*L is an actual semiample rational bundle; its class is nef. These facts meet F88’s resolution scope. Its normalization factorization is used to obtain the required connected-fiber application while retaining the original X and L. F therefore supplies one usc scalar psi with literal pullback equality at every analytic point, including minus infinity. Genuine source potentials are finite at the generic trivial valuation and have finite supremum. Birationality identifies that valuation, and analytic surjectivity transfers the upper bound and proves generic finiteness of psi. The subsequent argument uses only the stated properties of pi, so it works for every smooth projective resolution, not merely the one constructed by Temkin.

Original charts and reference. A sufficiently divisible actual tensor power qL gives a closed immersion into projective space. Consequently each nonempty U_i has original coordinate ring k[s_j/s_i]/I_i; no normalization or powers-only generating system is substituted. Canonical section norms are at most one, and the generating sections have a unit among their coefficients at every valuation center. Thus their maximum canonical norm is exactly one. The zero-weight global FS potential is consequently zero, and rho_i=−q^−1 log||s_i||_triv is exactly the canonical raw weight. Its pullback is the raw weight of the pulled frame, without any numerical-reference substitution.

The constant ratio gives rho_i≥0. Bounding rho_i bounds every affine generator. Polynomial degree bounds then bound every ring element, and the seminorm identities define a closed subset of a product of compact bounded intervals. This proves compactness of every sublevel set and hence properness of rho_i. Therefore u_i=psi+rho_i is usc, locally bounded above, generically finite, and satisfies u_i≤B+rho_i. A rational auxiliary exhaustion shift is harmless: it changes neither u_i nor its contacts, and its additive constant is cancelled when returning to canonical potentials. The original canonical global reference remains zero.

Actual86 conversion. On P_i=pi^−1(U_i), the pulled raw function is exactly phi+rho_i∘pi. P_i is smooth, integral, and finite type, and P_i→U_i is proper and birational. Properness here is relative; P_i need not be affine or proper over k. The local conversion is applied on affine source neighborhoods with the actual pulled frame. Its valid ample-perturbation pairs, directedness, and zero potentials in the actual difference bundles are those of the granted R86 body. No same-M ample approximation or target EP is inserted. The fixed auxiliary reference weights are finite on the compact generator-bounded neighborhoods, and the rational approximation and positive shifts produce finite rational AFS weights with the exact raw limit.

Sequence and contact hypotheses. Countability makes each source affine ring countable, so seminorm evaluation embeds its analytification into a countable product with a countable base. For a decreasing continuous net f_a on Q, each set {inf_a f_a<r}, r rational, is the union of {f_a<r}. Countable subcovers, followed by successive upper indices, give a decreasing sequence with the identical pointwise infimum. All rational thresholds are retained, so this includes minus infinity; cofinality is unnecessary. Restriction to Int(Q) gives an ordinary common neighborhood. When a collar requires a compact set with a surrounding common open neighborhood, take a smaller compact inside Int(Q).

Each finite AFS maximum has a finite winning branch. A winning logarithmic branch has nonzero seminorm and becomes a regular unit on its principal neighborhood. Its positive rational slope and the same constant give a support below the maximum with equality at the tested point. A winning floor gives constant support. Vanishing branches are suppressed on a sufficiently small ordinary neighborhood; the remaining used logarithms are unit logarithms there. Rational shifts alter the weight and its support together. These are precisely the supplied contact conditions, rather than an inference from weak positivity.

The remaining C89 antecedents also hold throughout its proof. Nonempty open and principal-open restrictions retain the original ring, function field, generic finiteness, and the restricted proper witness. Finite positive combinations, maxima, and floors retain the local contact data on common neighborhoods for the finite tuple; signed tests use the accepted actual80 construction. Product operations have witness P_i×A^1→U_i×A^1. Their logarithmic branches are units where active, while their prescribed floors handle w=0. The product remains integral and relatively proper birational with smooth source. Original generators, localized inverse generators, and the product coordinate are retained. Under a finite map to a smooth affine base, monic equations bound the original generators by an affine FS exhaustion on that base; the positive trace weights and their fixed total degree preserve the upper bound. At the generic trivial valuation, nonzero algebraic logarithms vanish, so the required nontriviality persists. There is no requirement that the original potential be finite on every singular stratum: the unbounded cases are handled by the prescribed finite floors.

G87 applies to each specified smooth affine operation and its actual restricted witness. Its completion and domination preserve the raw reference and exceptional points. Common domination is required only for finitely many witnesses; the countable approximation sequence stays on one witness and creates no infinite domination demand. Singular-stratum steps in C retain the original weak input and its witness rather than asserting generically finite restriction to every stratum. The completed-residue-field curve comparisons in F and C use their granted local contact mechanisms, not a countable affine theorem over arbitrary completed residue fields.

Principal localization and final globalization. On D(f), the witness is the same witness restricted to D(f), and the localized exhaustion includes f^−1. The logarithmic penalty and floors therefore have the required contacts and upper growth. The removal construction retains C’s decreasing-tail-envelope treatment; it does not pretend that the penalties decrease as their coefficients tend to zero. For equality with the original input, every divisorial valuation of the same integral witness has generic algebraic support and thus lies over D(f). Shared floors, references, and genuine collars compare both functions there and then at all analytic points; letting the floors descend retains minus-infinity values. The last auxiliary logarithmic maximum uses the product witness already checked above. The repaired Rossi localization is used with its supplied z∈V condition. Thus principal localization and the final empty-bad-set step meet the repaired C body’s antecedents. Neither dense-open equality plus usc nor target EP replaces those steps. No further indispensable antecedent is left unstated.

First membership. C now applies to the original u_i and gives its original-ring regularization and original projective consequence. For each rational c>1, the canonical potential chi_i,c equals psi−(c−1)rho_i on U_i and minus infinity outside. Its boundary extension is usc because psi is globally bounded above and rho_i tends to infinity at the chart boundary. Its genuine class is the actual cL. At any analytic point, a coordinate with canonical norm one gives rho_i=0. Every other chart contribution is at most psi. Hence max_i chi_i,c=psi exactly, including when psi is minus infinity. Finite-maximum closure gives psi∈PSH(cL). For c_m decreasing to one, apply [BJ4.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4#page=47) to the constant scalar sequence psi in classes c_m c1(L). It is decreasing and generically finite. This proves genuine L-membership before any EP on X. The individual chart extensions increase with m and are not the sequence used for this closure.

Identification and compactness. Genuine pullback follows from BJ4.7; birationality ensures its generic finiteness. F and first membership give surjectivity, and analytic surjectivity gives injectivity and equality of the actual suprema. The two divisorial coordinate sets are identical on the common function field: composition gives divisors over X from models over Y, and a common birational domination preserves the valuation of a divisor over X. This argument is independent of EP. Pointwise divisorial topologies therefore make pullback and its inverse continuous. The normalized spaces are homeomorphic. The smooth integral source is connected and its class is nef, so [BJ5.20–5.21](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4#page=61) give normalized compactness. Transporting that compactness and applying [general-projective BJ5.11](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1801.08229v4#page=58) proves target EP. BJ5.13 is not used to establish this identification or first membership.

Quantifiers, bindings, and retained scope. No step imposes a further condition on the countable algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, the original reduced irreducible geometrically unibranch projective target, or its actual ample rational L. Dimension zero is the single-point case: potentials are constants and the normalized space is a singleton; positive-dimensional IBP is unnecessary. Thus every target and polarization in E is covered. C means the continuation96 repaired body and its binding, including its localization correction; F means the exact roots92+93 body; R and G retain their roots90 and91 scopes. Smooth projective source is the retained interpretation, not smooth morphism. Increasing extracted indices need not be cofinal, shifted supports keep identical constants, and closure uses the constant scalar family. These are harmless binding clarifications, with no substantive repair of continuation99 required. Once E is discharged, section5 is available only as an application of precisely granted actual86, retaining its original varieties, raw mass and energy calibration, and after-EP normalization scope. No root98, author84, pending P13.2, full-paper grant, or original P16.1 closure enters this verdict.

passages.statement: Let Z be reduced projective over an algebraically closed trivially valued field. Its canonical line-bundle metrics have center-frame norm one and continuous global-section norms in [0,1]. A decreasing net φ_i∈PSH(θ_i), with θ_i→θ in N¹(Z) and generically finite pointwise limit φ:Zan→R∪{−∞}, has φ∈PSH(θ). PSH(θ) is closed under finite maxima and real constants. For morphisms f:W→Z of such varieties, generically finite f*φ belongs to PSH(f*θ). On irreducible Z, supφ=φ(v_triv)<∞. PSH(θ) carries pointwise convergence on divisorial valuations (BJ1.24,4.5,4.7,4.12,4.20).
